paragraphs: Adal, Ḥullin 134a: see Rashi, a foolish man named ben Tadal, from 'uncircumcised lips.' Arukh, Ben Arel: some read Adal with dalet; he was not precise in his teachings. Thus, if ben Adal teaches it, there is no concern for error since he gives a reason. 'My father and teacher read ben Gadal'—in my opinion it should read Tadal—an initialism for ten da'atekha lomar, 'give your attention to saying': attend to his words, since he gives a reason. [Quoted and narrator readings remain distinct.]
